reasons.reason: With a constant rotation rate, the angle swept is just rate times time, and 180 degrees per second over half a second works out to 90 degrees that the controller has to correct.
Stabilizing means the rotation rate ramps down from 180 degrees per second to zero, so the average rate is 90 per second, and over half a second that sweeps out 45 degrees.
A Doppler shift appears when the distance between star and observer is changing, and a line displaced toward red means the star is closing that gap and heading toward Earth.
Redshift means the observed wavelength is longer than the laboratory value, and Doppler stretching of wavelengths happens when the source is receding, so the star must be moving away from us.
Range goes as the sine of twice the launch angle, and that sine peaks when twice the angle equals ninety degrees, so the best launch angle is 45 degrees.
A lower launch keeps more of the speed horizontal, and at 30 degrees the horizontal component stays large while there is still enough lift to travel, which gives the longest distance before landing.
Side by side, the two resistors share the current between two paths, so the combination behaves like the average of the paths, which means adding the resistances and dividing by two.
In parallel the reciprocals add, so one over R equals one over R1 plus one over R2, and combining and flipping that fraction gives the product of the resistances over their sum.
A full circular loop gives μ₀I over 2R at its center, and a semicircle is exactly half of that loop, so the field at the center is half of the full-loop value.
Current goes out along the curved half and comes back along the straight diameter, and at the center those opposing contributions cancel by symmetry, so no net magnetic field remains there.
With constant speed there is no tangential acceleration at all, so the only acceleration left is centripetal, pointing toward the center with magnitude v squared divided by R.
The particle turns through angle at a rate of v divided by R, and since acceleration here measures how fast the motion changes direction, that turning rate gives its magnitude.

Doubling the current heats the lattice and raises its resistance along with it, and through Ohm's Law that extra resistance multiplies with the larger current, so the loss grows fourfold rather than twofold.
Power is the rate at which the field does work on carriers, and doubling the current doubles both the carrier flow and their drift speed and collision rate, and those two factors multiply to four.

Diffusion depends on the concentration difference driving molecules across and on how many molecules are available to move, and doubling the gradient raises both, so the rate goes up by a factor of four.
Fick's Law makes the diffusion rate directly proportional to the concentration gradient when area and thickness stay fixed, so doubling the gradient just doubles the rate of glucose crossing.
Using Q equals m c ΔT, the 10 degree rise times 4186 gives 41,860 joules per kilogram step, and scaling that up for the tank's water puts the total in the hundreds of thousands of joules.
Heat equals mass times specific heat times temperature change, so 1000 kg times 4186 times 10 degrees comes to roughly forty-two million joules for the whole storage tank.
Setting the derivative 4ax³ minus 2bx to zero gives the origin as an equilibrium point, and it sits at the center of this symmetric potential, where the particle settles with no net force.
The force vanishes where 4ax³ minus 2bx equals zero, giving x squared equal to b over 2a, and the second derivative 12ax² minus 2b is positive there, so those points are minima.
When the liquid's refractive index matches the glass, light meets no change in index at either lens surface, so nothing bends and the lens has no focusing power, making its focal length infinite.
A lens surrounded by a denser medium loses part of its bending power, and a liquid of index 1.5 cuts that power roughly in half, so the 20 cm focal length doubles.
Constant speed means zero net force along the slope, so mg sin θ equals μ mg cos θ, and dividing one by the other leaves the friction coefficient equal to the tangent of the angle.
Kinetic friction depends on the normal force, which on an incline is mg cos θ, and at steady speed the coefficient tracks that normal component, which ties it to the cosine of the angle.
Ten years contains two doubling periods of five years each, so the population of 100 doubles once to 200 and then doubles again to 400 foxes.
Each five-year doubling adds the original 100 foxes over again, so after the first period there are 200 and after the second period there are 300 in total.
A seed stays aloft only if it sinks more slowly than rising air lifts it, and terminal velocity climbs with mass, so beyond some mass the seed falls faster than updrafts can carry it.
Pappi and wings exist precisely to raise drag on the seed, and the drag coefficient sets how much air resistance the seed can generate for its mass, so it caps how heavy a dispersed seed can be.

The rms speed scales as the square root of temperature over molar mass, and at higher temperature the added energy is shared among translational and rotational motion, so translational speed only rises by root two.
The rms speed equals the square root of 3kT over m, so it scales with the square root of absolute temperature, and the square root of four is two.
